PullRequest.Title: chat: Add Copilot connectors as an authenticated customization source
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Adds an independently gated, authenticated Copilot Connectors source to the customization Marketplace and MCP management UI.

- Keeps connector discovery and consent separate from the anonymous GitHub Feed and MCP Gallery. Desktop requests use a scoped native channel with typed operations, bounded responses, cancellation, and per-request credentials; web uses the workbench request path.
- Preserves normal default-account sign-in scopes. Generic catalog browsing uses an ordinary GitHub session when supported. **Check Connection** and connection actions explicitly request missing connector permission for the same account; rollout-time HTTP 403 responses remain recoverable and never trigger passive consent.
- Composes connector results with other Marketplace sources using bounded ranked search and round-robin browse. One source failing, requiring sign-in, or being disabled does not hide healthy sources.
- Shows connected connector MCP servers under **Installed** and products under **Connectors**, with status-aware actions, details, explicit empty states, and user/workspace MCP precedence.
- Gates connector discovery and Copilot session availability on the default-off `chat.customizations.copilotConnectors.enabled` setting. Marketplace visibility remains independently controlled by `chat.customizations.marketplace.enabled`.
- Scopes session-time support to the Copilot Agent Host provider. VS Code retains the pre-session catalog and consent UI, while the bundled Copilot runtime owns session-time connector reconciliation, validation, managed MCP projection, credentials, collision handling, and lifecycle through `session.rpc.connectors.*`.
- Awaits runtime reconciliation before a Copilot session becomes available, so a connector that was just connected is usable in the first fresh session. Reconciliation failure is non-fatal to ordinary Copilot chat.

VS Code does not project connector endpoints or forward GitHub credentials to them. Credential delivery remains runtime-owned and endpoint-bound.

## Validation

- 1,064 changed-file unit tests pass locally (1 existing pending).
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` passes.
- Changed-file ESLint passes.
- Copilot Agent Host runtime-MCP lifecycle replay passes.
- Twelve connector/MCP component fixtures render without errors and remain stable in dark and light themes, including the empty Connectors tab and connector detail.
- Live verification connected Microsoft Learn Docs, created a completely fresh Copilot Agent session, invoked the runtime-managed `microsoft_docs_search` tool, and returned an official Microsoft Learn result. The connector was disconnected after validation.

## Manual test

1. Toggle Marketplace visibility separately from the public GitHub Feed and Copilot Connectors settings. With Marketplace off, verify Overview and legacy MCP management remain available. With Marketplace on, verify Discover and each enabled source independently.
2. Search, browse, filter, paginate, and fail or disable each source independently. Healthy results must remain available and retry must restart from the first page.
3. Start signed out, sign in with ordinary GitHub scopes, and browse the generic connector catalog without a connector-consent prompt when the backend permits it. Use **Check Connection** or **Connect** to explicitly upgrade the same account. Verify cancellation and recoverable rollout-time HTTP 403 behavior.
4. Connect and disconnect a connector. Verify its status and details, its connected MCP servers under **Installed**, and user/workspace MCP precedence.
5. Create a fresh Copilot Agent session immediately after connecting and invoke one of the connector's MCP tools. Disable the connector experiment and verify fresh Copilot sessions no longer expose connector tools.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The duplicate synchronous calls and full rebuild behavior are directly visible in the changed method with no timing or control-flow assumptions.
Findings.PerformanceResource: DOM nodes, list rows, buttons, hover/listener objects, layout work, and image elements
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The duplicate cost grows with the loaded result/card count and occurs every time the Discover page transitions from hidden to visible.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Extra synchronous UI work and allocation when switching to Discover, increasing avoidable latency and GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The existing branch rendered once when cached content was shown; when a catalog load was needed, loadCatalog rendered the loading state itself.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new unconditional render() runs after the branch, so the cached branch calls render twice back-to-back, and the loading branch also renders once inside loadCatalog before this second call.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 1783 unconditionally invokes this.render() while the unchanged else branch at line 1781 already does so, and loadCatalog also synchronously renders its loading state.
Findings.Title: Remove the second Discover render when the page becomes visible
Findings.Impact: Opening or returning to Discover rebuilds the same result list or clears and recreates all browse sections/cards twice before scheduling layout, which can make section switching less responsive on populated pages.
Findings.Evidence: setVisible() lines 1777-1783 calls render() in the else branch and then immediately calls it again unconditionally. render() invokes renderSearchResults() or renderBrowse() and layout(); renderSearchResults replaces the whole list, while renderBrowse clears browseSections and recreates sections, cards, buttons, hovers, listeners, and images for loaded catalog entries.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep exactly one render path: remove the unconditional call or remove the branch-local call and only render explicitly when loadCatalog does not already render.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The call path, request interval, timeout, full-catalog network boundary, response bound, and per-connector concurrency are explicit in the changed code; only the typical number of simultaneously pending connectors is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: HTTPS catalog requests, response bytes, JSON parsing, and connector object allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each connect or disconnect operation performs a full catalog GET immediately and then every 2 seconds for up to 5 minutes, so one unresolved action can issue about 150 GETs and N simultaneous connector actions can issue about 150×N requests for the same account catalog.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Excessive network traffic and repeated parsing/allocation, with contention that can delay status updates and other workbench requests.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no connector connect/disconnect polling path and therefore no repeated full-catalog request per pending connector action.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new connect loop calls refresh() on every iteration; refresh bypasses the 60-second getConnectors cache and sends a new authenticated query. The disconnect loop repeats the same pattern, while installation deduplication is keyed per connector rather than per shared catalog.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 367 invokes this.refresh(operation.token) inside the new 2-second/5-minute connect polling loop; the same added construction appears in disconnect().
Findings.Title: Coalesce connector status polling across pending operations
Findings.Impact: If authorization remains open or several connectors are connected from Discover in parallel, VS Code repeatedly downloads and parses the same catalog (responses are allowed up to 5 MiB) every two seconds per operation for as long as five minutes.
Findings.Evidence: connect() lines 365-372 repeatedly await refresh(), and disconnect() has the same loop. refresh() line 323 calls request({ type: 'query' }); request() line 495 crosses ICopilotConnectorsRequestService, whose native implementation performs GET /plugins with cache disabled and buffers/parses the response. The 2-second interval and 5-minute timeout bound this at roughly 150 catalog reads per unresolved operation. CustomizationMarketplaceInstallService uses getConnectorOperationKey(resource), allowing different connector names to run concurrently, and CopilotConnectorsService has no in-flight catalog-refresh coalescer (its Throttler is only for Agent Host refresh).
Findings.Recommendation: Use one account-scoped, cancellable polling/coalescing loop for all pending connector names (or at minimum coalesce in-flight refresh calls), apply backoff, and let cancellation unsubscribe one operation without cancelling a refresh still needed by others.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The synchronous critical path and per-launch multiplicity are explicit. refreshCatalog:true and the runtime-owned connector service establish the catalog refresh boundary; exact backend latency and runtime cache behavior are the remaining magnitude uncertainties.
Findings.PerformanceResource: runtime RPC/IPC calls and connector catalog network requests
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The cost is paid once for every created or resumed Copilot SDK session, including sessions recreated after connector/configuration changes; concurrent session launches each perform their own four-call sequence.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Higher chat/session startup latency because the first turn cannot proceed until the runtime refreshes and reconciles the connector catalog.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, _finalizeSession completed after script-safety and sandbox setup and performed no connector capability, authentication, account, or catalog-reconciliation RPCs.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every connector-enabled create/resume now synchronously awaits getCapabilities(), getStatus(), getAllUsers(), and reconcile({ refreshCatalog: true }) before wrapping and exposing the session.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 774 explicitly requests refreshCatalog:true from the runtime inside an awaited method newly inserted into _finalizeSession for every create/resume.
Findings.Title: Do not force a remote catalog refresh for every session launch
Findings.Impact: With connectors enabled, every new or resumed chat is placed behind a forced connector catalog refresh, so normal first-message latency inherits remote catalog latency even when connector membership has not changed since the previous session.
Findings.Evidence: _createSession and both resume paths now call _finalizeSession with a launch plan; _finalizeSession awaits _reconcileCopilotConnectors before returning. Lines 749-774 issue three sequential runtime RPCs followed by reconcile with refreshCatalog:true. CopilotAgentSession.initializeSession awaits launcher.launch, and CopilotAgent._refreshSessionConfiguration destroys/resumes sessions before a send when configuration is dirty, placing this work directly on session availability and first-turn paths.
Findings.Recommendation: Track catalog freshness per runtime account/change generation and request a remote refresh only for the first launch or after membership/auth invalidation; subsequent sessions should reconcile against the runtime's cached catalog (while still projecting servers per session). Coalesce concurrent launches for the same account.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, return to, or search the AI Customization Discover page
Scenarios.CriticalPath: setVisible either starts catalog loading or uses cached entries, then synchronously renders the result/browse DOM and lays it out. A cold connector-source query must complete before connector cards are available; local rendering is then on the UI critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GET of the Copilot connector catalog (/plugins), with a response bounded at 5 MiB and JSON parsing/validation bounded to 1,000 entries
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One connector GET per cold/expired discovery query; zero on a successful 60-second warm cache hit
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Discover had no Copilot connector source or connector catalog request before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold connector cards wait for the request; other discovery sources execute concurrently.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Loaded catalog/result cardinality (connector responses are capped at 1,000, and the aggregate page can include other marketplace sources). The added duplicate render scales with every displayed row/card on each visibility transition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Marketplace sources are queried concurrently by the discovery model, but connector lookup is one catalog operation. The two render calls are strictly serial synchronous work on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CopilotConnectorsService reuses a successfully loaded connector catalog for 60 seconds on getConnectors(); a cold or expired query makes one request. Failed loads are not success-cached. The duplicate rendering occurs for both warm data and the loading state, independent of cache warmth.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: setVisible's branch and trailing render calls, and renderBrowse/renderSearchResults rebuilding behavior, are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of loaded cards and per-card browser layout cost varies, so the duplicate-render finding is low severity; the two full render invocations are unconditional and certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity repeated synchronous UI rendering at the added trailing render call; the single cold catalog request itself is bounded and cached and is not independently a regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Connect or disconnect one or more Copilot connectors from customization UI
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation authorizes, refreshes the catalog, sends one mutation, and cannot complete until polling observes the target state. Every poll performs authentication lookup plus a full catalog request and parse.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated full-catalog GET /plugins followed by up-to-5-MiB buffering, JSON parse, and validation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Approximately one immediate GET plus one every 2 seconds, up to about 150 per unresolved operation; multiplies across pending distinct connector names
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector lifecycle polling or repeated connector catalog reads existed before this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each GET is serially required for that operation's next status check and completion; concurrent operations contend independently.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Connector connect PUT or disconnect DELETE
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector mutation endpoint was invoked before this feature.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to begin the state change; its completion precedes polling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the GitHub authentication session used to authorize each connector request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Called for every mutation and every polling refresh, though provider-side session state may itself be warm
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector operation performed this repeated authentication lookup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Precedes each network request in the polling loop.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of simultaneously pending distinct connector names and time until the service reflects each state. At a 2-second interval for a 5-minute deadline, each unresolved operation performs about 150 post-mutation catalog GETs, plus the initial refresh.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each individual polling loop serializes its own requests, but the marketplace install service deduplicates only by connector key. Distinct connector operations run concurrently with no account-wide limiter or shared in-flight refresh.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The normal 60-second catalog cache is deliberately bypassed because every poll calls refresh(). There is no shared refresh promise or negative cache; requests from overlapping operations do not coalesce.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: interval, deadline, refresh bypass, network request, response bound, and per-connector concurrency are all directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Backend propagation usually may finish before the deadline, and users may connect only one connector at a time; the high request cadence and lack of cross-operation coalescing remain explicit, supporting medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity missing coalescing: every pending operation independently downloads and parses the same account catalog on a fixed 2-second loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a Copilot chat session, including recreation after connector configuration changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session creation/resumption now awaits _finalizeSession, which sequentially awaits connector capabilities, auth status, user selection, and reconcile(refreshCatalog:true) before returning the SDK session. AgentSession initialization and a first send that requires a stale session restart cannot progress past launch until these calls finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Runtime RPCs for connectors.getCapabilities, gitHubAuth.getStatus, account.getAllUsers, and connectors.reconcile
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Four sequential RPCs for every connector-enabled create/resume
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Session finalization performed no connector-related runtime RPC sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All are awaited before the session is returned and can service the first turn.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh the runtime's connector catalog as requested by connectors.reconcile({ refreshCatalog: true })
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Requested once per session create/resume, including independently launched sessions
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No connector catalog refresh was requested during session launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The awaited reconciliation places catalog freshness on session initialization's critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of independently created/resumed SDK sessions. The fixed cost is four serialized runtime calls per launch, with a forced catalog refresh on each final reconciliation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The four connector calls are serialized within one session. Separate session launches have no visible account-scoped coalescer and can independently execute the sequence.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The changed call explicitly sets refreshCatalog:true, so it does not opt into a stale/cached catalog reconciliation. No cross-session freshness generation or coalescing is present in the launcher; runtime-internal caching details are unknown.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all caller paths, sequential awaits, and the session-launch critical path are directly traced; only runtime-internal network duration/coalescing is uncertain.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact runtime implementation and warm backend latency are not visible here, but the explicit forced-refresh contract and synchronous per-launch placement are clear; this limits severity to medium rather than negating the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity repeated boundary work because every session launch forces connector catalog reconciliation rather than sharing catalog freshness across sessions.

Scenarios.Scenario: Show the Installed MCP/customization list with connected Copilot connectors
Scenarios.CriticalPath: When the MCP section is visible, the widget updates installed definitions; the connector source reads the catalog, locally filters connected connectors, maps them to MCP definitions, and the widget renders them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authenticated GET of the full connector catalog when the shared cache is cold
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one per cold source query; zero during the 60-second warm-cache window, not one per displayed connector
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The Installed view had no Copilot connector catalog source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold connector subsection waits for this catalog read; filtering and rendering afterward are local.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of installed/connected definitions, bounded connector catalog size, and local record count used to merge installation state.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Installed-definition providers are aggregated; connector filtering/mapping is local. There is no per-connector network call or subprocess spawn in this path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Connector definitions use CopilotConnectorsService.getConnectors(), so a successful catalog read is shared for 60 seconds. A cold view may make one catalog GET; a warm view makes none.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source registration, cache behavior, and local filtering are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size and other installed-definition provider cost vary, but this path has bounded cardinality and a shared successful-result cache.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the cold boundary is one cached catalog request rather than per-row fan-out, and no concrete independently harmful regression was established.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 56 changed files and relevant callers. Submitted three diff-caused findings: account catalog polling is not coalesced across connector operations; session launch forces catalog reconciliation on every create/resume; and Discover visibility performs two synchronous full renders. Cold/warm cache behavior, effective concurrency, and IPC/network boundaries were traced for Discover, connector lifecycle, session launch, and Installed-list workflows. No qualifying regression-fix learning record was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
